touches.text: Runs a proof as its own process and writes a validation record (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon).

It is the READY TO MERGE ONTO MAIN step of the pipeline: everything's proved, and merging implies pushing it up. With a branch per ticket (3.3.6), commits on the branch are as often as we like; the inspector is the step at ready to merge. Checking what a change touched belongs here; nothing hangs off the git post-commit hook.

Once build_inspector moves into CodeMother, code outside her reaches it over the bus: the 18 crossing calls in transitions.py, the other code sites and the 82 proofs that run a sieve over themselves. No published client tool, no fifth exception. Akien 2026-11-13, on Q#88: "over the bus. that's what it's for?"
The only way to the database. WHY: the authentication is wrapped up in it, and every table has exactly one owner who gates every write; an ownerless table can't be made (Postgres refuses it).
Publishes a client tool (connect, read, write, query ...) that talks to the database over its socket, no bus hop: faster (2.3.7.1.1).

Every box runs its own instance of the database proxy, and everything on that box talks only to it (Akien, Q#113, 2026-11-14; 4.3.1.5.1.4.1.1). Each box's proxy is its own instance (1.3.4), so this agrees with 5.5.3.8 ("a device runs on one box"): no instance is duplicated, the class has one instance per box, like the foundational set of 5.5.3.8.1. WHY: the local read is fast, and the cache it fills is every box's backup. -amm; the fit with 5.5.3.8 - akienasus_cc_0
import_sieve: one parse of every .py into an import graph; what reaches what. WHY: enforces "only the proxy reaches the host/database" and RULE 1 by physics. USERS: CodeMother, the inference proxy.

The RULE 1 check is a path check: code inside device bar may not import cairn.devices.foo (anything not under cairn.devices.bar), except a tool foo publishes (cairn.devices.foo.tools.<x>, its charter saying published_by_device). Inside one device there is one owner, so nothing is checked there. A charter's public_interface describes what the component offers (modules, functions, bus verbs, commands); the check does not read it. Akien 2026-11-09 (Q#77): "wouldn't it be easier (for the python code anyway) to see if the imports do not include other device paths?"
